q: Natural proofs (Razborov-Rudich, 1994) are a framework for proving circuit lower bounds. A lower bound proof is 'natural' if it uses a property P of Boolean functions that is:
opts: Useful (functions outside circuit class C satisfy P), large (P holds for 2^{Ω(n)} functions), and constructive (P is computable in polynomial time)
exp: Razborov-Rudich: a natural proof against P/poly would break pseudorandom generators (which exist if OWFs exist). Most known lower bound techniques (switching lemma, random restrictions) are natural, suggesting they cannot prove P ≠ NP. This 'natural proofs barrier' explains why circuit lower bounds are hard.
